purpose: Plan, evaluate, and execute the design of clothing for men and women, from customer brief and trend research through silhouette, pattern, construction, fit, grading, and collection development to a complete production handoff, as a subdomain node in a knowledge-searcher meta-KB.
assumptions: scope is garment and collection design for menswear and womenswear, not footwear, accessories, or textile manufacturing
no observed dataset is supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors
the design phase ends at a costed, complete production handoff; bulk manufacturing is out of scope
nodes are concrete fashion-design work units bounded to one high-effort session
exclusions: footwear, millinery, and hard accessory design
textile fiber and fabric manufacturing engineering
retail merchandising operations and store execution
garment manufacturing line management and bulk production

competency_questions.question: Who is the garment for, at what price tier and occasion, and what single wearer outcome must it achieve?
What seasonal trend and market direction should shape this collection for the customer?
How is the concept expressed in a coherent palette and sketched design language?
What silhouette and proportion realize the design on the target body?
How is the garment patterned, draped, and fit-verified before production?
How do menswear and womenswear fit differ for this garment, and which block applies?
Which fabric and grain plan suit the silhouette, season, price, and intended drape?
What seams and finishes make the garment durable and clean within the fabric and price tier?
How is the approved fit graded across the size range without losing fit at the extremes?
How is the range planned and edited into one cohesive, well-architected collection?
What complete handoff package lets a factory produce the garment correctly?
How are cost, feasibility, and seasonal timing reconciled before the collection is committed?

glossary.definition: a quick illustrated figure used to explore garment designs on the body
a flat, to-scale technical drawing of a garment with construction callouts
the overall outline, shape, and volume of a garment on the body
a basic body-fitting pattern template from which styles are developed
two-dimensional pattern pieces drafted from blocks and measurements
shaping fabric directly on a dress form to develop a three-dimensional pattern
the direction of fabric threads that governs drape, stretch, and hang
the 45-degree direction across the fabric grain that gives fluid stretch and drape
a test garment in inexpensive fabric made to check fit and shape
scaling a base pattern across sizes using grade rules that preserve fit
a complete specification package a factory uses to produce a garment
the planned mix of styles, options, and price points across a collection

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from established fashion-design literature (Jenkyn Jones, Fashion Design; Aldrich, Metric Pattern Cutting for Women's Wear) and standard apparel design, pattern-cutting, fit, and collection-development practice; no measured dataset supplied.
does_not_support: observed garment sell-through or fit-pass rates
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Fix who the garment is for, the price tier, season, occasion, and the single wearer outcome before any sketch or pattern.
contradictors: designer who sketches with no customer in mind

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the target customer, price tier, season, or occasion changes

pros.claim: every silhouette, fabric, and fit choice inherits one clear wearer
pros.example: a streetwear hoodie targets a different body and budget than a tailored suit

cons.claim: a wrong customer misdirects the whole garment and the range
cons.example: cutting a slim tailored fit for a relaxed-fit market

failure_modes: intent stated as a vague mood not a wearer outcome
price tier or body type assumed wrong
acceptance_tests: intent is one sentence naming wearer, occasion, and price tier
customer profile names body type and budget
revisit_triggers: target customer or price tier changes

nodes.definition: Gather seasonal trend, color, and competitor signals and translate them into a directional point of view for the customer.
contradictors: designer who copies a single runway look wholesale

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the season turns or a new dominant trend signal appears

pros.claim: direction is grounded in the market not personal taste alone
pros.example: spotting a rising color before competitors stock it

cons.claim: over-indexing on trend dates the garment fast
cons.example: chasing a micro-trend that fades before delivery

failure_modes: trend copied not interpreted for the customer
research stops at one runway season
acceptance_tests: direction names a point of view distinct from a single copied look
opportunity gap is specific to the target customer

nodes.definition: Assemble images, textures, and references into a coherent visual concept that anchors the collection's story and aesthetic.
contradictors: designer who skips concept and sketches at random

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the concept fails to read as one coherent story

pros.claim: the board keeps every later choice on one aesthetic
pros.example: textures on the board justify fabric choices later

cons.claim: a pretty board with no edit gives no usable direction
cons.example: a board of 200 images that means nothing

failure_modes: board is decorative not directional
concept not translatable into garments
acceptance_tests: concept stated in one sentence a stranger can apply
board edits to a coherent aesthetic, not a scrapbook

nodes.definition: Lock the seasonal color palette and the proportion each color holds across the range so the collection reads as one story.
contradictors: designer who adds colors with no palette discipline

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the palette clashes with the concept or fails in the customer's market

pros.claim: a disciplined palette makes the range cohere and merchandise
pros.example: three core colors plus two accents tie the range together

cons.claim: too many colors fracture the story and inventory
cons.example: ten unrelated colors that never merchandise as a set

failure_modes: palette has no proportion plan
colors chosen that the customer rejects
acceptance_tests: palette has a stated proportion per color
palette reads coherently against the concept board

nodes.definition: Translate the concept into illustrated garment ideas on a figure to explore silhouette and proportion before technical work.
contradictors: designer who jumps to pattern with no exploration

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when sketches stop matching the concept or proportions read wrong

pros.claim: cheap exploration before costly pattern and sample work
pros.example: ten croquis filter to two strong silhouettes

cons.claim: beautiful sketches that ignore real construction mislead later steps
cons.example: a draped illustration that no flat pattern can realize

failure_modes: croquis proportions distort the real body
sketch ignores how the garment will be built
acceptance_tests: selected designs trace to the concept and palette
proportions are readable on a real figure scale

nodes.definition: Draw flat, to-scale technical drawings with construction callouts so the garment can be patterned and made consistently.
contradictors: designer who hands a maker only an artistic sketch

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the flat fails to communicate construction or scale to the patternmaker

pros.claim: a precise flat makes pattern and sample reproducible
pros.example: callouts specify seam type and topstitch so samples match

cons.claim: a vague flat forces the maker to guess and rework
cons.example: missing a pocket spec causes a wrong first sample

failure_modes: flat not to scale
construction details omitted
acceptance_tests: flat is to scale with front and back views
every seam, closure, and detail is called out

nodes.definition: Decide the overall shape, volume, and proportional balance of the garment relative to the body and the wearer's intent.
contradictors: designer who fixes details before the overall shape

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the silhouette no longer suits the body type or the wearer outcome

pros.claim: the silhouette is the first thing read and carries the design
pros.example: an A-line vs sheath changes the whole impression

cons.claim: detailing a wrong silhouette wastes pattern and sample work
cons.example: adding pockets to a silhouette that should be reconsidered

failure_modes: details decided before silhouette
proportion ignores the body type
acceptance_tests: silhouette decided before seam and detail work
proportion suits the named body type
revisit_triggers: body type or fit target changes
fabric drape forces a shape change

nodes.definition: Apply the differing block shapes, ease, and balance conventions that distinguish menswear and womenswear fit for the target body.
contradictors: designer who reuses one block for all bodies

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the body convention shifts between men's and women's blocks

pros.claim: the right gendered block makes the garment sit correctly on the body
pros.example: a women's bodice block adds bust shaping a men's block omits

cons.claim: using the wrong block convention breaks fit at the source
cons.example: drafting a men's jacket on a women's block misplaces the balance

failure_modes: one block reused across both conventions
ease borrowed from the wrong convention
acceptance_tests: block matches the menswear or womenswear target
ease and balance follow the convention for that body
revisit_triggers: target body or gender convention changes
fit feedback contradicts the block choice

nodes.definition: Choose fabrics by fiber, weight, hand, and drape that suit the silhouette, season, price, and care requirements.
contradictors: designer who picks fabric only by look

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the fabric fails the silhouette, season, price, or care need

pros.claim: fabric makes or breaks how the silhouette drapes and wears
pros.example: a stiff cotton holds an A-line a soft jersey cannot

cons.claim: a wrong fabric forces a redesign late and is costly to swap
cons.example: ordering a fabric that pills or is out of budget

failure_modes: fabric chosen by look not behavior
care or cost ignored until late
acceptance_tests: fabric hand and weight suit the silhouette
fabric meets price, season, and care targets
revisit_triggers: fabric goes out of stock or budget

nodes.definition: Plan how fabric grain and bias govern drape and hang so pieces are cut on the correct grain for the intended fall.
contradictors: designer who cuts off-grain without intent

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when garments hang or twist wrong due to grain or bias choices

pros.claim: correct grain makes pieces hang and not twist
pros.example: a bias-cut skirt falls in a fluid drape a straight cut cannot

cons.claim: off-grain cutting twists seams and wastes fabric
cons.example: a panel cut off-grain pulls to one side after washing

failure_modes: grainline ignored on the lay
bias used where stability was needed
acceptance_tests: every pattern piece marks a grainline
bias use is intentional and stabilized where needed
revisit_triggers: drape reads wrong on the sample

nodes.definition: Draft two-dimensional pattern pieces from body blocks and measurements to realize the silhouette with correct ease and seam allowance.
contradictors: designer who skips pattern and cuts freehand

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the pattern fails to realize the silhouette or fit at first sample

pros.claim: a sound pattern is the engineering that makes the garment real
pros.example: accurate ease lets the sleeve set without puckering

cons.claim: a flawed pattern propagates fit errors into every sample and size
cons.example: a wrong armhole curve ruins every jacket cut from it

failure_modes: ease applied wrong for the fabric
seam allowance or notches inconsistent
acceptance_tests: pattern realizes the silhouette at correct ease
seam allowances, notches, and grain are consistent
revisit_triggers: fabric behavior forces an ease change

nodes.definition: Shape fabric directly on a dress form to develop or refine complex silhouettes that flat patterning cannot easily resolve.
contradictors: designer who forces every shape into flat pattern

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a complex silhouette cannot be resolved or transferred cleanly to a flat pattern

pros.claim: draping resolves organic shapes the flat method struggles with
pros.example: a cowl neckline is found faster on the form than on paper

cons.claim: draping in the wrong fabric weight misleads the final result
cons.example: draping in calico gives a fall the real silk will not

failure_modes: draped in a fabric unlike the final
toile not transferred accurately to pattern
acceptance_tests: draped in a fabric matching the final behavior
toile transfers to a usable flat pattern
revisit_triggers: toile reads wrong on the body

nodes.definition: Specify seam types, edge finishes, and internal construction so the garment is durable, clean inside, and appropriate to the fabric.
contradictors: designer who ignores how seams are sewn

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a seam or finish fails for the fabric, durability, or price

pros.claim: the right seam suits the fabric and survives wear
pros.example: a French seam finishes a sheer cleanly with no raw edge

cons.claim: a wrong finish puckers, frays, or blows the cost
cons.example: an overlock on a delicate sheer looks cheap and frays

failure_modes: seam type mismatched to fabric
finish raises cost beyond the price tier
acceptance_tests: seam types suit the fabric and stress points
finishes meet durability within the price tier

nodes.definition: Make and evaluate a first sample or toile on a fit model to verify fit, balance, and construction before committing.
contradictors: designer who skips fit and goes straight to production

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when fit, balance, or construction fails on the body at the fit session

pros.claim: the fit session catches errors before costly grading and production
pros.example: a sleeve binding is caught and corrected on the toile

cons.claim: approving a poor fit propagates the error to every size and unit
cons.example: signing off a twisted side seam ships it to all sizes

failure_modes: fit judged on a hanger not a body
corrections not fed back to the pattern
acceptance_tests: fit assessed on a fit model in motion
every fit comment maps to a pattern correction
revisit_triggers: fit model or base size changes

nodes.definition: Scale the approved base pattern across the size range using grade rules so fit is preserved at every size.
contradictors: designer who scales by a flat percentage

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the graded sizes lose the approved fit at the extremes

pros.claim: correct grading preserves the approved fit across all sizes
pros.example: shoulder grade keeps balance from XS to XL

cons.claim: flat scaling distorts fit at the range extremes
cons.example: linear grading makes the largest size pull at the bust

failure_modes: uniform scaling instead of true grade rules
extremes of the range not fit-checked
acceptance_tests: grade rules preserve fit at sampled sizes
range extremes are validated on a body or form
revisit_triggers: fit fails at an extreme size

nodes.definition: Plan the number and mix of styles, options, and price points so the line covers the customer's needs without redundancy.
contradictors: designer who designs pieces with no line plan

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the line has gaps or redundant options against the customer need

pros.claim: a planned range covers needs and price points efficiently
pros.example: tops, bottoms, and layers balanced to build outfits

cons.claim: an unplanned range over-indexes on hero pieces and leaves gaps
cons.example: five statement coats and no sellable basics

failure_modes: range over-weights statement pieces
price architecture has gaps
acceptance_tests: option mix covers the customer's outfit needs
price points span the intended architecture

nodes.definition: Edit the developed styles into one cohesive collection by removing weak pieces and tightening the shared design language.
contradictors: designer who keeps every piece regardless of fit to the story

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the collection reads as unrelated pieces not one story

pros.claim: a tight edit makes the collection read as one intentional story
pros.example: cutting two off-concept pieces sharpens the whole line

cons.claim: keeping weak pieces dilutes the story and the margin
cons.example: leaving a piece that fits no outfit weakens the range

failure_modes: no piece is ever cut
cohesion sacrificed to save effort
acceptance_tests: every retained piece shares the design language
weak or off-concept pieces are cut with rationale

nodes.definition: Align the collection's fabrics, weights, and delivery to the selling season and the critical-path calendar.
contradictors: designer who ignores the selling calendar

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when fabric weight or delivery misaligns with the selling season

pros.claim: the right weights land in store at the right time to sell
pros.example: linen pieces deliver for spring not after the season

cons.claim: a late or off-season delivery kills sell-through
cons.example: winter coats arriving in spring miss the window

failure_modes: fabric weight wrong for the season
delivery misses the critical path
acceptance_tests: fabric weights suit the selling season
milestones fit the critical-path calendar

nodes.definition: Cost each style against its price tier and confirm it can be made at the target margin, quantity, and quality.
contradictors: designer who ignores cost until it is too late

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a style misses its target margin or cannot be made at volume

pros.claim: costing keeps designs sellable at the target margin
pros.example: catching a costly trim before it sinks the margin

cons.claim: an over-cost design ships a loss or must be redesigned late
cons.example: an unbuyable lining choice forces a late re-spec

failure_modes: cost ignored until production
manufacturability not confirmed at volume
acceptance_tests: each style meets its target margin
construction is feasible at the planned quantity

nodes.definition: Compile flats, specs, measurements, fabric, trims, and grading into a complete tech pack so a factory can produce the garment.
contradictors: designer who hands a factory loose sketches

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the factory cannot produce the garment correctly from the pack

pros.claim: a complete tech pack makes production reproducible and reduces sampling rounds
pros.example: a precise BOM and POM table cuts back-and-forth with the factory

cons.claim: an incomplete pack causes wrong production and costly reworks
cons.example: a missing measurement spec yields a wrong bulk run

failure_modes: pack missing measurements or BOM
handoff lacks grading or fabric data
acceptance_tests: pack includes flats, POM, BOM, grading, and fabric
a factory can produce correctly without follow-up guessing

edges.why_related: the customer frames which trends matter
edges.benefit_of_coupling: research is filtered to the customer
edges.example: scanning trends with no target body
edges.resolution_rule: fix the customer before scanning trends

edges.why_related: direction feeds the concept
edges.benefit_of_coupling: concept is grounded in the market
edges.risk_of_conflict: a concept untethered from the market
edges.example: a board ignoring the season direction
edges.resolution_rule: set direction before the concept

edges.why_related: the concept anchors the palette
edges.example: random colors off the board
edges.resolution_rule: lock concept before palette

edges.why_related: the concept directs sketching
edges.example: croquis with no concept
edges.resolution_rule: concept before croquis

edges.why_related: palette colors the sketches
edges.benefit_of_coupling: sketches read in the real palette
edges.example: rendering a piece in a cut color
edges.resolution_rule: palette before rendering croquis

edges.why_related: the chosen sketch becomes the flat
edges.risk_of_conflict: flats drawn for a rejected sketch
edges.example: specing a design that was cut
edges.resolution_rule: select the sketch before drawing flats

edges.why_related: sketches surface the silhouette to commit to
edges.benefit_of_coupling: the silhouette is chosen with intent
edges.example: fixing details before shape
edges.resolution_rule: explore in sketch then commit silhouette

edges.why_related: the silhouette is realized on a gendered block
edges.example: a men's block for a women's shape
edges.resolution_rule: fix silhouette then choose the block

edges.why_related: the target body selects the block convention
edges.risk_of_conflict: a block mismatched to the wearer
edges.example: using a women's block for a menswear brief
edges.resolution_rule: let the customer set the block convention

edges.why_related: the silhouette demands a suitable fabric
edges.example: a soft jersey for a structured A-line
edges.resolution_rule: commit silhouette then pick fabric

edges.why_related: palette constrains fabric color and finish
edges.benefit_of_coupling: fabric is available in the palette
edges.example: a color that no mill stocks
edges.resolution_rule: check the palette against fabric availability

edges.why_related: fabric behavior governs grain and drape planning
edges.example: cutting a fluid silk on the wrong grain
edges.resolution_rule: pick fabric then plan grain

edges.why_related: the block is drafted into a pattern
edges.benefit_of_coupling: the pattern realizes the right fit
edges.example: a pattern off a mismatched block
edges.resolution_rule: confirm the block then draft the pattern

edges.why_related: the spec tells the pattern what to build
edges.example: drafting a collar with no callout
edges.resolution_rule: spec the flat before drafting

edges.why_related: complex silhouettes are resolved by draping
edges.benefit_of_coupling: the shape is found in three dimensions
edges.example: draping aimlessly on the form
edges.resolution_rule: set the silhouette then drape

edges.why_related: draping must use the real fabric behavior
edges.benefit_of_coupling: the toile predicts the final fall
edges.example: calico draping for a silk garment
edges.resolution_rule: drape in a fabric matching the final

edges.why_related: the pattern defines where seams and finishes go
edges.benefit_of_coupling: construction is planned on real seams
edges.example: choosing a seam with no panel layout
edges.resolution_rule: draft the pattern then spec seams

edges.why_related: the fabric limits which seams and finishes work
edges.risk_of_conflict: a finish that frays or puckers the fabric
edges.example: an overlock on a delicate sheer
edges.resolution_rule: let the fabric bound the seam choice

edges.why_related: the pattern is tested by the fit sample
edges.risk_of_conflict: approving fit with no real sample
edges.example: signing off fit on paper only
edges.resolution_rule: draft then sample for fit

edges.why_related: construction quality shows at the fit session
edges.benefit_of_coupling: seam issues are caught on the sample
edges.example: a binding fault found in bulk
edges.resolution_rule: construct then review at fit

edges.why_related: fit comments trigger a pattern correction
edges.benefit_of_coupling: the pattern is corrected before grading
edges.risk_of_conflict: endless fit loops with no convergence
edges.example: re-cutting the armhole each round forever
edges.resolution_rule: stop when fit passes acceptance tests or after max fit rounds

edges.why_related: only an approved base is graded
edges.example: grading a base that later fails fit
edges.resolution_rule: approve fit before grading

edges.why_related: grading feeds the tech pack size set
edges.risk_of_conflict: a pack with no graded set
edges.example: handing off one size only
edges.resolution_rule: grade before the tech pack

edges.why_related: the customer shapes the range plan
edges.risk_of_conflict: a range with no customer logic
edges.example: planning options no customer needs
edges.resolution_rule: fix the customer then plan the range

edges.why_related: direction informs the option mix
edges.example: planning against a stale direction
edges.resolution_rule: set direction before the option plan

edges.why_related: the plan is the basis for the edit
edges.benefit_of_coupling: the edit works against a target mix
edges.example: cutting pieces with no architecture
edges.resolution_rule: plan the range then edit

edges.why_related: shared silhouettes drive cohesion
edges.example: clashing shapes across pieces
edges.resolution_rule: align silhouettes for cohesion

edges.why_related: a shared palette unifies the collection
edges.example: a piece in an off-palette color
edges.resolution_rule: hold the palette across the edit

edges.why_related: the plan is sequenced to the season
edges.example: planning with no delivery dates
edges.resolution_rule: plan the range then time it

edges.why_related: fabric weight and lead time bound the season
edges.benefit_of_coupling: weights and timing suit the season
edges.example: linen pieces for winter delivery
edges.resolution_rule: let fabric bound the season plan

edges.why_related: construction drives the cost
edges.example: ignoring finish cost in the sheet
edges.resolution_rule: spec construction then cost it

edges.why_related: fabric choice changes the cost and margin
edges.risk_of_conflict: a fabric that breaks the margin
edges.example: an over-budget fabric sinking the style
edges.resolution_rule: feed fabric cost into the costing

edges.why_related: the price architecture sets the cost targets
edges.benefit_of_coupling: each style has a margin target
edges.example: no margin target for a style
edges.resolution_rule: set price architecture then cost

edges.why_related: unviable cost can force a piece to be cut
edges.risk_of_conflict: cost cuts hollow out the collection
edges.example: cutting so much the line collapses
edges.resolution_rule: stop cutting when the edit holds cohesion and margin

edges.why_related: a bold palette and a complex silhouette compete for attention
edges.risk_of_conflict: a piece that fights itself visually
edges.example: loud print on an intricate silhouette
edges.resolution_rule: let the design intent pick which leads; quiet the other

edges.why_related: the ideal fabric can exceed the cost target
edges.example: a luxe wool that breaks a mid-tier price
edges.resolution_rule: trade to the best fabric within the price tier or re-tier the style

edges.why_related: a draped toile is transferred to a flat pattern
edges.risk_of_conflict: draping that never becomes a pattern
edges.example: a toile left untransferred
edges.resolution_rule: transfer the toile to a pattern before drafting downstream

edges.why_related: flats and specs populate the tech pack
edges.example: handing off with no spec sheet
edges.resolution_rule: finalize flats then assemble the pack

edges.why_related: approved cost and BOM go into the pack
edges.risk_of_conflict: a pack with no costed BOM
edges.example: handing off uncosted materials
edges.resolution_rule: cost and approve before handoff

conflict_axes.trigger: the fabric that best serves the design exceeds the cost target
resolution_order: confirm the price tier
find the best fabric within budget
re-tier the style only if the design demands the fabric
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the price tier leads for commercial styles; quality leads only for hero or premium pieces with sign-off
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if no in-budget fabric serves the design and re-tiering is proposed
conflict_axes.example: a luxe wool needed for drape breaks a mid-tier coat's margin

conflict_axes.trigger: an extreme silhouette compromises real-body fit and comfort
resolution_order: state the wearer outcome
keep the silhouette wearable for that body
reserve extremes for runway or hero looks
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: wearable fit dominates for commercial garments; creative extremes are allowed only for show pieces
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if the silhouette cannot be made to fit the target body
conflict_axes.example: an exaggerated shoulder that no fit model can wear comfortably

conflict_axes.trigger: a hot trend conflicts with the brand's customer and identity
resolution_order: check the trend against the customer
adopt only trends the customer will buy
translate, do not copy
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the brand customer dominates; trends are filtered through brand identity, not adopted wholesale
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if adopting a trend would alienate the core customer
conflict_axes.example: a loud micro-trend that the core minimalist customer rejects

conflict_axes.trigger: a bold print and an intricate silhouette compete for the eye
resolution_order: decide which carries the design
quiet the other element
verify the piece reads cleanly
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the design intent picks the lead element; the secondary element is simplified to support it
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if neither element can be subordinated without losing the concept
conflict_axes.example: a busy floral on a heavily seamed bodice that fights itself

conflict_axes.trigger: a shape is faster or truer in one method than the other
resolution_order: assess the silhouette's complexity
drape organic shapes, draft geometric ones
transfer drape to a flat pattern for production
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: method follows the shape; complex organic shapes drape, structured geometric shapes draft, and all converge to a flat production pattern
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if neither method resolves the shape cleanly
conflict_axes.example: a cowl drapes faster than it drafts, a tailored panel drafts faster than it drapes

conflict_axes.trigger: adding options to cover needs dilutes the collection story
resolution_order: cover core customer needs first
cut pieces that break cohesion
add breadth only within the design language
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: cohesion dominates once core needs are met; breadth is added only when it preserves the story
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if covering a needed category would break the story
conflict_axes.example: adding ten colorways that fragment an otherwise tight capsule

conflict_axes.trigger: the calendar pressures shipping before fit is approved
resolution_order: protect the fit gate
compress non-fit steps first
slip the date before shipping a bad fit
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: fit approval dominates the calendar; the date slips before an unapproved fit ships
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if the date cannot be met without skipping fit approval
conflict_axes.example: pressure to grade before the toile fit is signed off

conflict_axes.trigger: elaborate finishing raises cost and production time
resolution_order: confirm durability needs
spend finish budget where it shows and wears
simplify finishes that blow the cost
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: durability and price tier dominate; decorative finishing is kept only where it serves wear or visible quality within budget
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if required finishing cannot fit the cost target
conflict_axes.example: hand-finished seams that triple the make cost of a basic

edge_cases.failure_mode: endless fit rounds with no approval
edge_cases.example: the armhole is re-cut every round and never signs off
edge_cases.detection_method: count fit rounds against the max and track residual error
resolution: escalate to a senior fit technician
accept the best fit or re-scope the design

edge_cases.trigger: the selected fabric is unavailable or late
edge_cases.failure_mode: a design committed to an unavailable fabric
edge_cases.example: the chosen mill discontinues the cloth mid-development
edge_cases.detection_method: confirm stock and lead time against the critical path before lock
resolution: slip the date if no equivalent exists

edge_cases.trigger: the approved fit breaks at the size extremes
edge_cases.failure_mode: largest or smallest sizes fit poorly
edge_cases.example: linear grading pulls the bust on the largest size
edge_cases.detection_method: fit-check sampled sizes at the range extremes
resolution: replace flat scaling with true grade rules

edge_cases.trigger: pieces are cut off the intended grain
edge_cases.failure_mode: seams twist and panels distort after wear or wash
edge_cases.example: a side panel cut off-grain pulls to one side
edge_cases.detection_method: check grainlines on the marker and on the sewn sample

edge_cases.trigger: the costed style misses its target margin
edge_cases.failure_mode: a style ships at a loss or is pulled late
edge_cases.example: a trim and fabric combination overruns the price point
edge_cases.detection_method: compare the cost sheet to the price-tier margin target

edge_cases.trigger: the tech pack is handed off missing data
edge_cases.failure_mode: the factory makes a wrong bulk run
edge_cases.example: a missing points-of-measure table yields a wrong bulk
edge_cases.detection_method: check the pack against a required-contents checklist before release
resolution: complete flats, POM, BOM, and grading
hold production until the pack is complete

edge_cases.trigger: pieces do not read as one collection
edge_cases.failure_mode: a fragmented line that does not merchandise
edge_cases.example: unrelated silhouettes and palettes across the range
edge_cases.detection_method: lay the line out and check shared silhouette, palette, and language

edge_cases.trigger: a runway look is copied wholesale
edge_cases.example: copying a designer look one-to-one for a different customer
edge_cases.detection_method: compare the design against the source and the brand point of view
resolution: translate the trend through brand identity

edge_cases.trigger: the toile is draped in an unrepresentative fabric
edge_cases.failure_mode: the final garment falls differently than the toile
edge_cases.example: a calico toile predicts a fall the silk will not give
edge_cases.detection_method: compare the toile fabric weight and drape to the final
resolution: adjust the pattern for the real drape

edge_cases.trigger: a cost-quality tradeoff is modeled as a prerequisite
edge_cases.failure_mode: a real tension is hidden as a dependency and never resolved
edge_cases.example: treating fabric-over-cost as an ordering rule instead of a conflict to resolve
edge_cases.detection_method: check that cost-quality tradeoffs appear as conflict edges or axes, not dependencies
resolution: model the tension as a conflict axis
keep the dependency only for true prerequisites

edge_cases.trigger: production is locked before fit is approved
edge_cases.failure_mode: a fit error is committed to bulk
edge_cases.example: the pack is released to the factory before the toile signs off
edge_cases.detection_method: verify fit approval status before any hard lock of the tech pack
resolution: block handoff until fit is approved

workflow.objective: fix the customer, intent, and market direction
acceptance_tests: intent names wearer, occasion, and price tier
direction is a point of view not a copy
workflow.do_first_because: nothing downstream is valid unless the customer and direction are fixed first

workflow.objective: build a coherent concept and lock the palette
acceptance_tests: concept is one applicable sentence
palette has a proportion plan
workflow.do_first_because: a locked concept and palette keep every later choice on one story

acceptance_tests: selected designs trace to the concept
silhouette suits the body type
workflow.do_first_because: committing silhouettes early prevents reworking detail and pattern later

workflow.objective: produce technical flats and choose the gendered block
acceptance_tests: flat is to scale with callouts
block matches the menswear or womenswear target
workflow.do_first_because: a precise flat and the right block make pattern work reproducible

workflow.objective: select fabric and plan grain and drape
acceptance_tests: fabric hand suits the silhouette
every piece has a grainline
workflow.do_first_because: fabric and grain must be settled before pattern and construction depend on them

acceptance_tests: pattern realizes the silhouette at correct ease
toiles transfer to a usable pattern
workflow.do_first_because: the pattern is the engineering that turns the design into a real garment

workflow.objective: spec construction and verify fit on a sample
acceptance_tests: seams suit the fabric and stress points
fit is approved on a body in motion
exit_criteria: fit is approved and construction is set
workflow.do_first_because: fit and construction errors must be caught before grading and production

workflow.objective: grade the approved pattern across the size range
acceptance_tests: grade rules preserve fit at sampled sizes
range extremes are validated
exit_criteria: the size range is graded and validated
workflow.do_first_because: only an approved fit may be scaled, and the extremes must hold the fit

workflow.objective: plan, edit, and time the collection
acceptance_tests: option mix covers customer needs
every retained piece shares the design language
exit_criteria: the collection is edited and timed
workflow.do_first_because: editing to cohesion and timing protects the story and the selling window

workflow.objective: cost the styles and hand off a complete tech pack
acceptance_tests: each style meets its margin target
the pack lets a factory produce without guessing
fit is approved before any hard lock
exit_criteria: the costed, complete pack is handed off
workflow.do_first_because: production must only start from a costed, complete, fit-approved pack

priority_rationale.notes: root intent all work inherits
direction feeds concept and range
concept anchors palette and sketch
palette colors design and fabric
sketch selects designs and silhouette
silhouette drives block, fabric, and cohesion
line architecture sets the commercial frame
block convention precedes pattern
flats spec the pattern and pack
fabric is costly to swap late and drives many steps
grain plan precedes cutting
the pattern is the core engineering of fit
draping resolves shapes feeding the pattern
construction precedes fit and cost
fit approval gates grading and production
grading precedes the tech pack
the edit protects the collection story
timing aligns delivery to the season
cost gates feasibility before handoff
the complete pack ends the design phase

dominance_rules.trigger: fit approval competes with the calendar
dominance_rules.rule: fit approval dominates over hitting the date
dominance_rules.required_action: slip non-fit steps or the date before shipping an unapproved fit
dominance_rules.example: grading is held until the toile signs off

dominance_rules.trigger: a desirable step lacks its prerequisite
dominance_rules.required_action: complete the prerequisite before the higher-value dependent step
dominance_rules.example: palette is locked before fabric color is chosen

dominance_rules.trigger: a trend conflicts with the brand customer
dominance_rules.rule: the brand customer dominates raw trend adoption
dominance_rules.required_action: translate the trend through brand identity or drop it
dominance_rules.example: a loud micro-trend the core customer rejects is dropped

dominance_rules.trigger: a creative extreme breaks real-body fit
dominance_rules.rule: wearable fit dominates creative extremes for commercial garments
dominance_rules.required_action: keep extremes for show pieces and ensure commercial fit
dominance_rules.example: an unwearable shoulder is reserved for the runway look only

dominance_rules.trigger: an ideal fabric breaks the price tier
dominance_rules.rule: the price-tier margin dominates fabric ambition for commercial styles
dominance_rules.required_action: find the best in-budget fabric or re-tier with sign-off
dominance_rules.example: a mid-tier coat uses a costed wool blend, not a luxe wool

dominance_rules.trigger: a sample passes informally but not QA
dominance_rules.rule: QA validation dominates the urge to lock
dominance_rules.required_action: pass acceptance tests before any soft or hard lock
dominance_rules.example: the tech pack is not hard-locked until completeness checks pass

dominance_rules.trigger: an irreversible or high-risk decision arises
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automation for irreversible or high-risk steps
dominance_rules.required_action: route fabric commitment, fit sign-off, and handoff to human review
dominance_rules.example: bulk production is not committed without a human go decision

dominance_rules.required_action: keep heuristic labels and do not claim observed without data
dominance_rules.example: metric estimates stay labeled heuristic with no fabricated measurements

dominance_rules.rule: cohesion dominates breadth once core needs are met
dominance_rules.required_action: cut pieces that break the design language
dominance_rules.example: an off-concept extra colorway is cut to keep the capsule tight

dominance_rules.trigger: an object is added with no source or link
dominance_rules.required_action: every node, edge, and claim references a source and a question
dominance_rules.example: no metric or edge is added without an evidence_ref

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the customer and intent before any design work
anti_rework_rules.rationale: designing for the wrong customer is reworked wholesale
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: sketching starts before the customer is named
anti_rework_rules.example: croquis drawn before the price tier is known

anti_rework_rules.rule: lock the concept before the palette
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a palette with no concept is redone when the concept lands
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: colors chosen before the concept exists

anti_rework_rules.rule: commit the silhouette before detailing and pattern
anti_rework_rules.rationale: detailing a wrong silhouette wastes pattern and sample work
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: details or pattern started before the shape is set
anti_rework_rules.example: adding pockets before the silhouette is decided

anti_rework_rules.rule: choose the gendered block before drafting the pattern
anti_rework_rules.rationale: drafting from the wrong block breaks fit at the source
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: pattern drafted before the block convention is set
anti_rework_rules.example: using a women's block for a menswear garment

anti_rework_rules.rule: settle fabric and grain before pattern and construction
anti_rework_rules.rationale: ease and grain depend on the fabric, so a swap forces re-drafting
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: pattern drafted before the fabric is chosen
anti_rework_rules.example: drafting ease for an unknown fabric weight

anti_rework_rules.rationale: grading an unapproved base propagates a fit error to every size
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: grading starts before the toile signs off
anti_rework_rules.example: scaling a pattern that later fails fit

anti_rework_rules.rule: cost and confirm feasibility before handoff
anti_rework_rules.rationale: handing off an over-cost or unmakeable style forces a late redesign
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: the pack is released before costing
anti_rework_rules.example: an uncosted BOM goes to the factory

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not hard-lock production before fit approval
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a production lock before fit commits any fit error to bulk
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: the pack is hard-locked before fit sign-off
anti_rework_rules.example: releasing bulk before the toile is approved

anti_rework_rules.rule: plan the range before editing the collection
anti_rework_rules.rationale: editing with no plan leaves gaps and redundant options
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: pieces cut or kept with no architecture
anti_rework_rules.example: editing the line before the option mix is planned

anti_rework_rules.rule: complete traceability before any hard lock
anti_rework_rules.rationale: locking untraceable artifacts hides ungrounded decisions
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a node or edge lacks a source or question link at lock
anti_rework_rules.example: hard-locking the pack with unlinked specs

iteration_protocol.trigger: the validator or a review reports a failure
iteration_protocol.detection: compare validation_report checks and review notes to thresholds
acceptance_tests: every failure mapped to a subsystem

iteration_protocol.detection: rank defects by risk and downstream impact
action: score each defect by risk and coupling
acceptance_tests: high-risk defects are addressed first
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: the queue is empty or only sub-threshold defects remain

iteration_protocol.trigger: a fix may affect locked or coupled work
iteration_protocol.detection: trace dependents and downstream artifacts of the change
action: map affected nodes, edges, and steps
acceptance_tests: all dependents of a change are identified

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect is routed for repair
iteration_protocol.detection: apply the fix in the owning subsystem
action: repair via the formula script or content fix
acceptance_tests: the targeted check now passes
no new failures introduced

iteration_protocol.trigger: new evidence or a fit result shifts importance
acceptance_tests: posterior change exceeds the revisit delta only when justified
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: posterior change is below the revisit delta

iteration_protocol.trigger: a high-risk or irreversible defect cannot be auto-repaired
acceptance_tests: a human decision is recorded for high-risk items

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new KB version is produced
iteration_protocol.detection: compare against the prior version's checks and counts
action: diff validation and metrics against the prior run
acceptance_tests: no check regresses without justification

human_review_required_for: tech-pack handoff and any irreversible production lock
re-tiering a style above its planned price

checks.repair_action: modeled fabric/cost and palette/silhouette tensions as conflict edges, not dependencies
fit->pattern correction kept as a feedback edge, not a dependency

test_cases.input_summary: the same silhouette must fit a man and a woman
the ideal wool breaks a mid-tier coat's margin
pressure to grade before the toile signs off
linear grading pulls the bust on the largest size
the range reads as unrelated pieces
the tech pack ships missing a POM table

change_triggers: target customer or price tier changes
version_increment_rules: increment on any hard-locked tech-pack change
increment when formulas or metric weights change
lock_downgrade_rules: downgrade dependents when an upstream node changes
downgrade on a failed fit or QC pass
downgrade when an evidence label is revised
human_approval_required_for: irreversible release of the tech pack
hard lock of the production pack
